GER 155.heading: GER155
GER 155.name: Critical Artificial Intelligence
GER 155.summary: Studies the history and theory of artificial intelligence through humanities analysis, including how machine-learning systems are constructed and their philosophical, political and cultural implications.

C LIT 155.heading: C LIT155
C LIT 155.name: Critical Artificial Intelligence
C LIT 155.summary: Studies the history and theory of artificial intelligence through humanities analysis, including how machine-learning systems are constructed and their philosophical, political and cultural implications.

CMPSC 25.heading: CMPSC25
CMPSC 25.name: Data Programming and Analytics for Artificial Intelligence
CMPSC 25.summary: Develops Python programming and data-analysis workflows for AI, covering acquisition, cleaning, transformation, simulation, visualization and statistical inference through projects.
CMPSC 25.prerequisites: CMPSC 9 or CMPSC 24 with a grade of C or better; and, Mathematics 3A or 2A with a grade of C or better (may be taken concurrently).

CMPSC 41.heading: CMPSC41
CMPSC 41.name: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science
CMPSC 41.summary: Introduces discrete mathematics through counting, sets, graph theory, elementary probability and number theory.
CMPSC 41.prerequisites: Computer Science 16 with a grade of C or better and Mathematics 4A with a grade of C or better.

CMPSC 42.heading: CMPSC42
CMPSC 42.name: Logic and Automata
CMPSC 42.summary: Introduces propositional and predicate logic alongside formal languages, automata and Turing-machine models of computation.
CMPSC 42.prerequisites: Computer Science 41; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only.

CMPSC 135.heading: CMPSC135
CMPSC 135.name: Mathematics of Artificial Intelligence
CMPSC 135.summary: Develops statistical, linear-algebra and optimization foundations for AI, including estimation, graph probability models, gradient methods, convex optimization, kernels and backpropagation.
CMPSC 135.prerequisites: Math 4A; CMPSC 25 or CMPSC 24; and ECE 139.

CMPSC 183.heading: CMPSC183
CMPSC 183.name: Ethics, Privacy, Fairness, and Bias in AI and Computing
CMPSC 183.summary: Examines responsible AI through privacy, bias, fairness, transparency and human oversight, using case studies and practical cloud tools for explainability and model monitoring.

CMPSC 187.heading: CMPSC187
CMPSC 187.name: Deep Learning
CMPSC 187.summary: Studies deep-learning principles, convolutional/recurrent/Transformer/graph architectures, loss design, training and inference with analysis and implementation.

CMPSC 184.heading: CMPSC184
CMPSC 184.name: Mobile Application Development
CMPSC 184.summary: Develops and deploys mobile applications using software design, development practices and testing tools.
CMPSC 184.prerequisites: Computer Science 56 or Computer Science 156; and Computer Science 130A.

CMPSC 153A.heading: CMPSC153A
CMPSC 153A.name: Hardware/Software Interface
CMPSC 153A.summary: Designs embedded software under real-time and resource constraints, using I/O protocols, interrupts and static/dynamic scheduling.
CMPSC 153A.prerequisites: Upper division standing in Computer Science, ComputerEngineering, or Electrical Engineering. Familiarity with C, FiniteAutomata, and Computer Architecture.

CMPSC 181.heading: CMPSC181
CMPSC 181.name: Introduction to Computer Vision
CMPSC 181.summary: Studies computer-vision methods for images and video, including segmentation, pattern recognition, motion, stereo, shape recovery and object recognition.
CMPSC 181.prerequisites: Upper-division standing in Artificial Intelligence, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.

ECE 139.heading: ECE139
ECE 139.name: Probability and Statistics
ECE 139.summary: Introduces probability and statistics, including conditional probability, Bayes rules, random variables, moments, Markov chains and hypothesis testing.
ECE 139.prerequisites: Open to Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering and pre-Computer Engineering majors only.

ECE 153A.heading: ECE153A
ECE 153A.name: Hardware/Software Interface
ECE 153A.summary: Designs embedded software under real-time and resource constraints, using I/O protocols, interrupts and static/dynamic scheduling.
ECE 153A.prerequisites: Upper division standing in Computer Engineering, Computer Science and Electrical Engineering. Familiarity with C, FiniteAutomata, and Computer Architecture.

ECE 180.heading: ECE180
ECE 180.name: INTRODUCTION TO DEEP LEARNING
ECE 180.summary: Introduces multilayer neural networks, perceptrons, associative memory, backpropagation, convolutional/recurrent networks and attention, with language and vision applications.
ECE 180.prerequisites: Open to EE, Computer Engineering and Computer Science with upper-division standing.

ECE 181.heading: ECE181
ECE 181.name: Introduction to Computer Vision
ECE 181.summary: Studies computer-vision methods for images and video, including segmentation, pattern recognition, motion, stereo, shape recovery and object recognition.
ECE 181.prerequisites: Upper-division standing in Artificial Intelligence, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Chemical Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.

ECE 186.heading: ECE186
ECE 186.name: Probabilistic Machine Learning
ECE 186.summary: Develops probabilistic machine-learning methods, including regression, inference, estimation, Markov models, expectation maximization and reinforcement learning, with implementation projects.

ME 107.heading: ME107
ME 107.name: Machine Learning
ME 107.summary: Formulates and implements machine-learning problems in Python, covering generalization, optimization, principal components, regression, support-vector machines and neural networks.
ME 107.prerequisites: ME 17; or consent of instructor Recommended preparation (not a required prerequisite): PSTAT 120A.

CMPSC 1A.heading: CMPSC1A
CMPSC 1A.name: Artificial Intelligence Seminar
CMPSC 1A.summary: Introduces foundational AI techniques and interdisciplinary applications through faculty seminars, readings and discussion.

WRIT 109ES.heading: WRIT109ES
WRIT 109ES.name: Writing for Environmental Studies
WRIT 109ES.summary: Analyzes and practices professional environmental writing, emphasizing audience, research, document design, collaboration and editing for topics such as water management and sustainability.
WRIT 109ES.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Not open for credit after English 109I.

CMPSC 9.heading: CMPSC9
CMPSC 9.name: Intermediate Python Programming
CMPSC 9.summary: Develops intermediate Python programming through object-oriented design, runtime analysis, data structures and software testing.
CMPSC 9.prerequisites: CMPSC 8 or CMPSC W8 or ENGR 3 or ENGR W3 or ECE 3 with a grade of C or better. Advisory Enrollment Comments: CMPSCW 9 is the online version of CMPSC 9

CMPSC 130A.heading: CMPSC130A
CMPSC 130A.name: Data Structures and Algorithms
CMPSC 130A.summary: Analyzes data structures and graph traversal, including correctness proofs, hash tables, heaps and balanced search trees.
CMPSC 130A.prerequisites: CMPSC 40 or CMPSC 41 or MATH 8 with a grade of C or better; CMPSC 24 or CMPSC 25 with a grade of C or better; PSTAT 120A or ECE 139 (may be taken concurrently with CMPSC 130A); open to Computer Science Department majors, and Electrical and Computer Engineering Department majors only. The Recommended Preparation field also lists PSTAT120AorECE139(concurrent allowed); the prerequisite field independently includes the same requirement.

CMPSC 130B.heading: CMPSC130B
CMPSC 130B.name: Algorithm Design and Analysis
CMPSC 130B.summary: Studies algorithm design and complexity using divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic-programming methods, recurrence analysis and NP-completeness.

CMPSC 165A.heading: CMPSC165A
CMPSC 165A.name: Artificial Intelligence
CMPSC 165A.summary: Introduces intelligent agents, heuristic search, knowledge representation, probabilistic reasoning, machine and reinforcement learning, and responsible AI.

CMPSC 165B.heading: CMPSC165B
CMPSC 165B.name: Machine Learning
CMPSC 165B.summary: Studies machine-learning techniques including neural networks, concept and decision-tree learning, genetic algorithms, Bayesian and analytical learning.
CMPSC 165B.prerequisites: Computer Science 130A. Recommended preparation (distinct source field): Computer Science 111.

CMPSC 188.heading: CMPSC188
CMPSC 188.name: Introduction to Natural Language Processing
CMPSC 188.summary: Studies statistical and neural language-processing methods, including language models, sentiment analysis, tagging and translation, with empirical corpus evaluation.
CMPSC 188.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CMPSC 130A, CMPSC 165A, and CMPSC 165B. Recommended preparation (distinct source field): Recommended preparation: CMPSC 138.

MATH 3A.heading: MATH3A
MATH 3A.name: Calculus with Applications, First Course
MATH 3A.summary: Develops differential calculus, limits, differentiation techniques and applications, with an introduction to integration and logarithmic/trigonometric functions.
MATH 3A.prerequisites: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam. Recommended preparation (distinct source field): Students with Advanced Placement Credit should contact the department. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Students who have completed Math 34A or 34LA will only receive 2 units for Math 3A. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2A or 3AS or have passed the AP Calculus AB or BC exams. Repeat Comments: If students earn a C- or lower in Math 2A, then Math 3A can be taken as a legal repeat as long as students get a qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam to take Math 3A.

MATH 3B.heading: MATH3B
MATH 3B.name: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
MATH 3B.summary: Develops integral calculus, integration techniques, sequences and series, with mathematical and physical applications.
MATH 3B.prerequisites: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C. Recommended preparation (distinct source field): Students with Advanced Placement Credit should contact the department. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Students who have completed Math 34B or 34LB will only receive 2 units for Math 3B. Not open for credit to students who have completed Math 2B or 3BS or have passed the AP Calculus BC exam. Repeat Comments: If students earn a C- or lower in Math 2B, then Math 3B can be taken as a legal repeat.

MATH 4A.heading: MATH4A
MATH 4A.name: Linear Algebra with Applications
MATH 4A.summary: Studies linear equations, matrices, determinants, vector spaces, transformations, eigenvalues and orthogonality.
MATH 4A.prerequisites: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 4B.heading: MATH4B
MATH 4B.name: Differential Equations
MATH 4B.summary: Studies first- and second-order differential equations, systems, nonlinear equations and stability.
MATH 4B.prerequisites: Math 4A or Math 4AI with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 6A.heading: MATH6A
MATH 6A.name: Vector Calculus with Applications, First Course
MATH 6A.summary: Develops multivariable and vector calculus, including vector-valued functions, double/triple integrals and changes of variables.
MATH 6A.prerequisites: Mathematics 4A (or 4AI) with a letter grade of C or better.

ENGL 146AI.heading: ENGL146AI
ENGL 146AI.name: Literature and/of Artificial Intelligence
ENGL 146AI.summary: Examines agency, human purpose and artificial entities through literary and philosophical questions about automation, cognition and machine intelligence.
ENGL 146AI.prerequisites: Writing 2 or upper-division standing. Credit may repeat only with different letter designations; catalog maximum six additional repeats/28units for the suffix family, not extra requirements for this course.

ENGL 146DS.heading: ENGL146DS
ENGL 146DS.name: Data Stories: Theory and Practice of Data-driven Narratives in the Digital Age
ENGL 146DS.summary: Applies humanities theories of narrative, genre and media to data journalism and visualization, culminating in a data-driven narrative project.
ENGL 146DS.prerequisites: Writing 2 or upper-division standing. Credit may repeat only with different letter designations; catalog maximum six additional repeats/28units for the suffix family, not extra requirements for this course.

ENGL 197.heading: ENGL197
ENGL 197.name: Upper-Division Seminar
ENGL 197.summary: A variable-topic seminar requiring a library-based project and research beyond primary course materials; current detailed topics are published by the English department.
ENGL 197.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 50 or 109 or English 10 or upper-division standing.

WRIT 1.heading: WRIT1
WRIT 1.name: Approaches to University Writing
WRIT 1.summary: Practices critical reading, analysis of academic discourse and rhetorical strategies for university writing. Earning C or better satisfies the entry-level writing requirement.
WRIT 1.prerequisites: The current course field requires an unsatisfied Entry Level Writing Requirement and an Analytical Writing Placement Exam score of 6 or lower. No credit after English 1, Writing 1LK or Writing 1E, or an AP English score of at least3. Maximum5units with no additional-credit repeats. Current university placement/CWP policy is separately reviewed; this course-field AWPE wording does not establish a universal examination obligation.

WRIT 1E.heading: WRIT1E
WRIT 1E.name: Approaches to University Writing for Engineers
WRIT 1E.summary: Practices academic reading, analysis, exposition and argument through examinations and revised papers, with attention to rhetorical strategies.
WRIT 1E.prerequisites: The current course field requires an unsatisfied Entry Level Writing Requirement and an Analytical Writing Placement Exam score of 6 or lower. Freshmen only; ECE, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Computer Engineering majors only. No credit after English 1, Writing 1 or Writing 1LK, or an AP English score of at least3. Maximum4units with no additional-credit repeats. AI is not among the named majors; no automatic exception is inferred. Current university placement/CWP policy remains separately reviewed.

WRIT 2.heading: WRIT2
WRIT 2.name: Academic Writing
WRIT 2.summary: Develops source synthesis, sustained argument and stylistic revision through academic reading and writing across disciplines.
WRIT 2.prerequisites: Satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing requirement or Linguistics 12 with a grade of "C" or better. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 2 or Writing 2E or 2LK or have passed AP English exam (Composition and Literature or Language and Composition) with a score of 4 or higher. Maximum 5 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 2E.heading: WRIT2E
WRIT 2E.name: Academic Writing for Engineers
WRIT 2E.summary: Develops source synthesis, sustained argument and stylistic revision using engineering reading and writing assignments.
WRIT 2E.prerequisites: Satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing requirement or Linguistics 12; freshmen only; open to ECE, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Computer Engineering majors only. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit if student has completed English 2, Writing 2LK, Writing 2 or has passed the AP English exam (Composition and Literature or Language and Composition) with a score of 4 or higher. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 50.heading: WRIT50
WRIT 50.name: Writing and the Research Process
WRIT 50.summary: Studies analytical research processes through writing in varied academic and professional communities; section topics differ.
WRIT 50.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit if student completed English 3, Writing 50E or 50LK or passed AP English exam (Composition & Lit. or Lang. & Composition) with a 5. See writing program for section descriptions. Maximum 5 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 50E.heading: WRIT50E
WRIT 50E.name: Writing and the Research Process for Engineers
WRIT 50E.summary: Studies analytical research processes and writing within engineering academic and professional communities.
WRIT 50E.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; freshmen only; open to ECE, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, and Computer Engineering majors only. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 3 or Writing 50 or 50LK or have passed the AP English exam (Composition and Literature or Language and Composition) with a score of 5. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 105AI.heading: WRIT105AI
WRIT 105AI.name: Writing and Generative AI
WRIT 105AI.summary: Studies writing with generative AI through communication strategy, self-reflection, knowledge development and ethical decisions.
WRIT 105AI.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK ; upper-division standing Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 105CD.heading: WRIT105CD
WRIT 105CD.name: Writing with Code
WRIT 105CD.summary: Combines textual composition and coding in interactive narratives, visualizations, games and web documents; no coding background is assumed.
WRIT 105CD.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 105CW.heading: WRIT105CW
WRIT 105CW.name: Writing in Community
WRIT 105CW.summary: Practices research and community writing for local organizations, attending to audiences, genres and reflective communication.
WRIT 105CW.prerequisites: Writ 2 or Writ 2E or Writ 2LK or Exam: AP 36 >=4 or Exam: AP 37 >=4 or Exam: WAIV AW >= 1 or Exam: IB BL >= 6 or Exam: IB E >= 6; upper division standing. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 105M.heading: WRIT105M
WRIT 105M.name: Multimedia Writing
WRIT 105M.summary: Analyzes and produces multimedia writing for digital publication, with reflection on communication choices.
WRIT 105M.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Advisory Enrollment Comments: WRIT W 105M is the online version of WRIT 105M. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 105PD.heading: WRIT105PD
WRIT 105PD.name: Writing and Public Discourse
WRIT 105PD.summary: Studies civic and political writing and produces research on public discourse and policy communication.
WRIT 105PD.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 105PS.heading: WRIT105PS
WRIT 105PS.name: Writing for Public Speaking
WRIT 105PS.summary: Develops researched speeches, presentation scripts and supporting media for academic and professional audiences.
WRIT 105PS.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 105S.heading: WRIT105S
WRIT 105S.name: Writing About Sustainability
WRIT 105S.summary: Researches and composes writing about sustainability, emphasizing how words and images communicate across audiences.
WRIT 105S.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 105SW.heading: WRIT105SW
WRIT 105SW.name: Science Writing for the Public
WRIT 105SW.summary: Practices translating scientific research and concepts for nonspecialist audiences through established and digital media.
WRIT 105SW.prerequisites: Writ 2 or Writ 2E or Writ 2LK or Exam: AP 36 >=4 or Exam: AP 37 >=4 or Exam: WAIV AW >= 1 or Exam: IB BL >= 6 or Exam: IB E >= 6; upper division standing. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 107B.heading: WRIT107B
WRIT 107B.name: Business and Administrative Writing
WRIT 107B.summary: Practices concise business communication, collaborative reports, proposals and employment documents with visual and oral components.
WRIT 107B.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109C or Writing 109EC. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 107EP.heading: WRIT107EP
WRIT 107EP.name: Writing for Environmental Professions
WRIT 107EP.summary: Practices professional environmental communication through audience research, document design, collaboration and editing.
WRIT 107EP.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 107G.heading: WRIT107G
WRIT 107G.name: Professional Writing for Global Careers
WRIT 107G.summary: Develops professional documents for international business, government and nonprofit contexts, including collaborative research.
WRIT 107G.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Repeat Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed WRIT 109GS between Spring 2005 and Summer 2011. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 107J.heading: WRIT107J
WRIT 107J.name: Journalism and News Writing
WRIT 107J.summary: Practices reporting and news composition for print, broadcast and digital media, including interviewing, editing and ethics.
WRIT 107J.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed WRIT 109JW Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 107L.heading: WRIT107L
WRIT 107L.name: Legal Writing
WRIT 107L.summary: Develops legal analysis and clear written argument in case briefs, memoranda, correspondence and appellate documents.
WRIT 107L.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109D or WRIT 109L Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 107M.heading: WRIT107M
WRIT 107M.name: Magazine Writing for Publication
WRIT 107M.summary: Practices interviews, reviews and feature articles for publication, with attention to audience, editing and deadlines.
WRIT 107M.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Repeat Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed WRIT 105MW between Summer 2003 and Spring 2010. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 107T.heading: WRIT107T
WRIT 107T.name: Technical Writing
WRIT 107T.summary: Develops instructions, manuals and online documentation using task analysis and communication design for technology users.
WRIT 107T.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 107WC.heading: WRIT107WC
WRIT 107WC.name: Writing Web Content
WRIT 107WC.summary: Analyzes rhetorical choices and creates professional web, email and social-media content.
WRIT 107WC.prerequisites: Writ 2 or Writ 2E or Writ 2LK or Exam: AP 36 >=4 or Exam: AP 37 >=4 or Exam: WAIV AW >= 1 or Exam: IB BL >= 6 or Exam: IB E >= 6; upper division standing Advisory Enrollment Comments: WRIT 107WC is a legal repeat of WRIT W 107WC Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 109ED.heading: WRIT109ED
WRIT 109ED.name: Writing for the Teaching Professions
WRIT 109ED.summary: Examines current educational theory, practice and policy through research, discussion and analysis for prospective teachers.
WRIT 109ED.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 106WP. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 109HP.heading: WRIT109HP
WRIT 109HP.name: Writing for Health Professions
WRIT 109HP.summary: Develops academic and professional health-care writing through research and discussion of contemporary issues.
WRIT 109HP.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109M. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

WRIT 109ST.heading: WRIT109ST
WRIT 109ST.name: Writing for Science and Technology
WRIT 109ST.summary: Practices scientific and technical reports, proposals and research writing, including graphics, editing and document design.
WRIT 109ST.prerequisites: Writing 2 or 2E or 2LK; upper-division standing. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed English 109A. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 110.heading: CMPSC110
CMPSC 110.name: Introduction to Research in Computer Science
CMPSC 110.summary: Students formulate a computing research question, read technical literature and communicate a team research proposal through writing and presentations.
CMPSC 110.prerequisites: Computer Science 40 and Computer Science 32; consent of instructor. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 111.heading: CMPSC111
CMPSC 111.name: Introduction to Computational Science
CMPSC 111.summary: Numerical methods cover matrix computations, linear systems, eigenvalue and singular-value decompositions, and optimization using scientific software.
CMPSC 111.prerequisites: Mathematics 4B with a grade of C or better; Mathematics 6A with a grade of C or better; Computer Science 24 with a grade of C or better. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 110A. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 132.heading: CMPSC132
CMPSC 132.name: Algorithms Engineering
CMPSC 132.summary: Students analyze computational problems, estimate algorithm performance and implement correct, efficient solutions.
CMPSC 132.prerequisites: No required-prerequisite field is published in this current record; this is not a statement that no preparation is required. Recommended preparation (not a required prerequisite): CMPSC 24 and CMPSC 40. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for enrollment or credit to students who have previously completed "CMPSC 190A: Special Topics - Algorithms Engineering" in Winter 2023 or Winter 2024 with Prof Daniel Lokshtanov. Repeat Comments: CMPSC 132 is a legal repeat of "CMPSC 190A: Special Topics - Algorithms Engineering" offered in Winter 2023 and Winter 2024 with Prof Daniel Lokshtanov. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 134.heading: CMPSC134
CMPSC 134.name: Randomized Algorithms
CMPSC 134.summary: Randomized algorithms are developed and analyzed to understand their efficiency and simplicity.
CMPSC 134.prerequisites: CMPSC 130B with a letter grade of B or better. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for enrollment or credit to students who have previously completed "CMPSC 190A: Special Topics - Randomized Algorithms" in Spring 2023 with Prof Eric Vigoda. Repeat Comments: CMPSC 134 is a legal repeat of "CMPSC 190A: Special Topics - Randomized Algorithms" offered in Spring 2023 with Prof Eric Vigoda. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 138.heading: CMPSC138
CMPSC 138.name: Automata and Formal Languages
CMPSC 138.summary: Formal-language models progress from finite automata and regular expressions to context-free languages, pushdown automata and computability.
CMPSC 138.prerequisites: Computer Science 40 or Computer Science 41 with a grade of C or better; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 140.heading: CMPSC140
CMPSC 140.name: Parallel Computing
CMPSC 140.summary: Parallel computing covers shared-memory and cluster architectures, GPUs, threading, message passing, performance tuning and distributed data processing.
CMPSC 140.prerequisites: MATH 4A with a grade C or better; and, CMPSC 32 or CMPSC 130A. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 110B. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 148.heading: CMPSC148
CMPSC 148.name: Computer Science Project
CMPSC 148.summary: Teams develop, test and demonstrate software using engineering practices, interface design, libraries and reliability techniques.
CMPSC 148.prerequisites: Computer Science 32 with a grade of C or better; open to Computer Science majors only. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 48 with a grade of C or better. Repeat Comments: CMPSC 148 is a legal repeat of CMPSC 48. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 154.heading: CMPSC154
CMPSC 154.name: Computer Architecture
CMPSC 154.summary: Computer architecture examines processors, memory, controllers, peripherals, interrupts and hardware/software tradeoffs.
CMPSC 154.prerequisites: Computer Science 32 with a grade of C or better; Computer Science 64 with a grade of C or better. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have received credit for ECE 154 or ECE 154A or ECE 154B. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 156.heading: CMPSC156
CMPSC 156.name: Advanced Applications Programming
CMPSC 156.summary: Advanced software development covers generic programming, exceptions, memory management, development tools, testing, code review and legacy software.
CMPSC 156.prerequisites: Computer Science 24 and 32 with a grade of C or better; open to Computer Science and Computer Engineering majors only. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 20. Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 56 with a grade of C or better. Repeat Comments: CMPSC 156 is a legal repeat of CMPSC 56. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 160.heading: CMPSC160
CMPSC 160.name: Translation of Programming Languages
CMPSC 160.summary: Compiler construction covers lexical and syntax analysis, type checking, runtime environments, intermediate code and implementation tools.
CMPSC 160.prerequisites: Computer Science 64 or Electrical Engineering 154 or Electrical Engineering 154A; Computer Science 130A; and Computer Science 138; open to computer science and computer engineering majors only. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 162.heading: CMPSC162
CMPSC 162.name: Programming Languages
CMPSC 162.summary: Programming-language concepts include scope, parameter passing, storage, control flow, types, modularity, inheritance and several programming paradigms.
CMPSC 162.prerequisites: Computer Science 130A and 138; open to computer science and computer engineering majors only. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 170.heading: CMPSC170
CMPSC 170.name: Operating Systems
CMPSC 170.summary: Operating systems cover processes, communication and synchronization, input/output, file systems and memory management.
CMPSC 170.prerequisites: Computer Science 130A; and, Computer Science 154 or ECE 154A (may be taken concurrently); open to computer science, computer engineering or electrical engineering majors only. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 171.heading: CMPSC171
CMPSC 171.name: Distributed Systems
CMPSC 171.summary: Distributed systems cover communication, naming, logical time, consistency, fault tolerance and recovery across networked machines.
CMPSC 171.prerequisites: Computer Science 130A. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 151. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 172.heading: CMPSC172
CMPSC 172.name: Software Engineering
CMPSC 172.summary: Students plan and implement a software project while studying requirements, design, testing, maintenance and project management.
CMPSC 172.prerequisites: Computer Science 130A. Open to Computer Science or Computer Engineering majors only, or by consent of department. Recommended preparation (not a required prerequisite): Computer Science 130B. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who completed CMPSC 189A Winter 2003-Summer 2021. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 174A.heading: CMPSC174A
CMPSC 174A.name: Fundamentals of Database Systems
CMPSC 174A.summary: Database foundations include relational models and query languages, integrity constraints, data modeling, dependencies and normalization.
CMPSC 174A.prerequisites: Computer Science 130A. Recommended preparation (not a required prerequisite): Students are strongly encouraged to complete Computer Science 56 or Computer Science 156 prior to enrolling in Computer Science 174A. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 174B.heading: CMPSC174B
CMPSC 174B.name: Design and Implementation Techniques of Database Systems
CMPSC 174B.summary: Database implementation covers query optimization, indexing, transactions, concurrency, logging, recovery and distributed databases.
CMPSC 174B.prerequisites: Computer Science 130B. Recommended preparation (not a required prerequisite): Students are strongly encouraged to complete Computer Science 56 or Computer Science 156 prior to enrolling in Computer Science 174B. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 176A.heading: CMPSC176A
CMPSC 176A.name: Introduction to Computer Communication Networks
CMPSC 176A.summary: Networking covers layered protocols, error detection, flow control, routing, medium access and high-speed communication.
CMPSC 176A.prerequisites: CMPSC 32 with a grade of C or better; PSTAT 120A or ECE 139; open to computer science, electrical engineering, and computer engineering majors only. Recommended preparation (not a required prerequisite): PSTAT 120B. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed Computer Science 176 or ECE 155 or ECE 155A. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 176B.heading: CMPSC176B
CMPSC 176B.name: Network Computing
CMPSC 176B.summary: Internet applications are built using socket programming, networking and web technologies for distributed services.
CMPSC 176B.prerequisites: Computer Science 176A. Advisory Enrollment Comments: Not open for credit to students who have completed ECE 155B or 194W. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.

CMPSC 176C.heading: CMPSC176C
CMPSC 176C.name: Advanced Topics in Internet Computing
CMPSC 176C.summary: Advanced Internet topics include wireless/mobile networks, multimedia, security, multicast, service quality, IPv6 and caching.
CMPSC 176C.prerequisites: Computer Science 176A. Recommended preparation (not a required prerequisite): Computer Science 176B, PSTAT 120A. Maximum 4 units; no additional-credit repeats.
